newsitem.title: USA: Best Buy sees net up, same-store sales down.
newsitem.headline: Best Buy sees net up, same-store sales down.

text.p: Electronics superstore retailer Best Buy Co Inc, whose business has slumped due to a lack of hot consumer product rollouts recently, said it expects higher earnings but lower same-store sales for fiscal 1998.
Minneapolis-based Best Buy said in a government filing that intense competition in retailing and a dry spell of hit electronic gadgets will pressure sales for the second year in a row.

Nonetheless, the company still expects earnings to increase, although it anticipates a loss for the first half, according to the filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, made Wednesday.

"As a result of the higher comparable-store sales decline and seasonally slower volumes, the company anticipates reporting a loss in the first half of the year," Best Buy said. "However, improved earnings are expected for the year as a whole."
For fiscal 1997 ended March 1, Best Buy earned $1.7 million, or $0.04 a share. That compared with earnings of $48 million, or $1.10 a share, in the prior year.
The retailer's comparable-store sales, or sales at stores open a year, fell five percent in fiscal 1997.

Despite sluggish sales, Best Buy intends to focus on higher-margin items such as service contracts and major appliances, which are more profitable than PCs, for example, the retailer said. It also will offer consumer financing packages and devote more floor space to products with fatter margins, it said.
Digital Satellite Systems were popular last year and helped lift sales, but not enough to make up for weak demand for other video goods, Best Buy said.

The rollout of Digital Versatile Discs this spring and the development of digital TV "represents opportunity to generate new interest in this category in the years ahead," the filing said. But the new products are pricey and are expected to have only a modest impact on sales this year.
